answer: Behavioral co-occurrence clustering tracks each identity’s action mix across contexts; a classifier flags accounts whose feature vectors form a tight ridge separating them from organic users. Enforcement then merges flagged identities into one meta-account and re-scores shared history, so each fresh persona needs a distinct behavioral footprint. The attacker’s cost is per identity: maintaining a unique, coherent activity thread over months. A single mesa of near-identical profiles collapses under this audit.
